en: The Sūtra on the Devaputra Jvālanānta Receiving the Three Refuges and Attaining Escape from the Evil Realms,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master [of] Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India.
Translated by the Imperial Preceptor, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fātian, by imperial decree: Thus have I heard:
At one time the World-Honored One was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
At that time, there was a devaputra named Jālinīprabha, whose celestial retribution was nearing its end with only seven days remaining; he thus first manifested the five signs of decay:

his body lost its majestic splendor and became covered in filth, the flower garlands upon his head all withered and shriveled, a foul odor issued from his limbs, and sweat flowed profusely from both armpits.
At that time, because of this, Jāṅgulī was distressed and took no pleasure in her seat; she rolled upon the ground, weeping in sorrow, and spoke these words:
"Alas! How bitter!"
Alas! The Lake Mānasa; alas!
Alas! The bathing pool; alas!
Alas! The precious chariots, the Coarse and Wicked Delight Grove, and other such parks—alas, we shall no longer sport there! Alas!
Alas! The pārijātaka flower shall never again be plucked; the ground of soft, variegated jewels shall never again be trodden upon. Alas!
“Alas! The celestial maidens, so upright, exquisite, and beautiful, who have always attended upon us, now depart from us.
At that time, another son of heaven, having witnessed this event, went to the abode of Śakra and said:
“O Lord of Devas!
When the five signs of decay appeared for that Cakravartin king, with only seven days remaining of his life, he rolled upon the ground, weeping in sorrow,
and spoke these words:”
"Alas! Alas! Manojñā, the bathing pool and other such ponds!"
Alas! Alas! The jeweled chariots, the Coarse and Wicked Grove, the Joyful Mixed Grove, and all such parks—there we shall no longer sport.
Alas! Alas!
The pārijātaka flower shall never again be plucked; the ground of variegated jewels and softness shall never again be trodden upon.
Alas! Alas! The celestial maidens, so dignified and exquisite, who have always attended upon me, now depart from me.
"O Lord of Devas!
Having seen this, my heart is deeply pained; therefore, I have come to inform you.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of Devas, out of compassion, went to the abode of Jāmbālaka and addressed him, saying:
“Devaputra! Why is it that you, a worthy one, are rolling upon the ground, weeping in sorrow, and speaking of various matters of suffering, thereby moving and distressing those who see you?”
At that time, when Tārkṣya heard these words, he rose from the ground, adjusted his robes, assumed a solemn countenance, and stood with palms joined, addressing Śakra:
"Lord of Devas!..."
My life span now remains for only seven days; after my death, due to my past karma, I shall fall into the great city of Rājagṛha in Jambudvīpa and receive the body of a pig.
"Lord of Devas!
Having received that body, for many years I have consumed excrement and filth; observing this suffering, I am therefore filled with grief.
When Śakra, Lord of Devas, heard these words, his heart was moved by profound compassion, and he addressed the Devaputra Jālinīprabha, saying:
“Wise one! You should take refuge in the Triple Gem with a sincere heart.
You should speak thus:”

“I take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One that is free from desire; I take refuge in the Saṅgha, the Honored One among assemblies.
Then, out of fear of death and dread of rebirth as an animal, the devaputra Cāṇūra spoke to Śakra, saying: “Kauśika!

"I now take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One free from desire; I take refuge in the Saṃgha, the Honored One among assemblies.
At that time, having received the three refuges, that devaputra’s mind remained uninterrupted until the end of his life.
According to the laws of the devas, those of inferior wisdom possess limited vision and cannot perceive what lies above.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, observed the place where that son of heaven had been reborn: had he been born in the great city of Rājagṛha in Jambudvīpa to receive the body of a pig, or would he not receive such a body?
Exhausting the range of his divine eye, he observed but did not see him.
He further observed the realms of animals and hungry ghosts, yet still did not see him;
he further observed the human world within the Sahā universe, yet still did not see him.
He searched as far as the Heaven of the Four Great Kings and the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, yet he could not see him anywhere.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of Devas, having failed to find him, felt doubt and uncertainty arise in his mind.
Thereupon Śakra went to the Jeta Grove, approached the World-Honored One, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

That Devaputra Cāru-dharma, with the five signs of impending death manifest before him and his life span limited to seven days, rolled upon the ground, weeping in sorrow and lamenting his various sufferings, moving all who saw him to grief.
At that time, I went there, and having seen this, I asked him:
"Why is it, worthy one, that you are weeping and distressed, so emaciated and haggard?"
At that time, Jālanāma addressed me, saying:
"My life now has but seven days remaining.
After my death, I shall fall into Jambudvīpa and be born in the city of Rājagṛha with the body of a pig, where for many years I shall feed upon various kinds of filth and excrement."
Upon hearing these words, my heart was filled with profound compassion, and I said to him:
"Now, O worthy one, if you wish to be liberated from this suffering, you must take refuge in the Triple Gem."
He spoke these words:

"I take refuge in the Buddha, the most honored among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the most honored among those free from desire; I take refuge in the Saṅgha, the most honored among assemblies.
At that time, Jaṭila, out of fear of death and dread of rebirth as an animal, addressed me, saying:

"I now take refuge in the Buddha, the most honored among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the most honored among those free from desire; I take refuge in the Sangha, the most honored among assemblies.
At that time, Jāṅgulī took the Three Refuges and only then passed away.
“World-Honored One!
I do not now know where that Jāṅgulī-dharmā has been reborn.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with his perfect and universal knowledge, addressed Śakra, saying:
“Kauśika! The Devaputra Cāṇūra has now been born in the Tuṣita Heaven, where he enjoys the pleasures of the five senses.
When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, heard these words of the Buddha, he leaped for joy with a heart full of gladness; his faculties were perfected, and he spoke this verse before the Buddha:
"If one takes refuge in the Buddha, one shall not fall into the evil realms;
having cast off this human body, one shall obtain a celestial body.
If one takes refuge in the Dharma, one shall not fall into the evil realms."
Having cast off this human body, one shall obtain a celestial body;
if one takes refuge in the Saṅgha, one will not fall into the evil realms,
and having cast off this human body, one shall obtain a celestial body.
He further spoke in verse:
"With a sincere heart, one takes refuge in the Buddha;
whatever that person may obtain, whether by day or by night, the mind of the Buddha shall constantly be recollected."
With sincere heart, one takes refuge in the Dharma;
whatever that person may obtain, whether by day or by night, shall be constantly sustained by the power of the Dharma.
With sincere heart, one takes refuge in the Sangha; whatever that person may obtain, [shall likewise be sustained].
"Whether by day or by night, the majesty of the Saṅgha shall always provide protection.
When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had spoken this verse, the World-Honored One confirmed it, saying: "So it is, so it is."
“Taking refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, one will certainly not fall into the evil realms;
having cast off this human body, one shall surely attain a celestial body.”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"If the two syllables 'Bud-dha' reach one's tongue, It is equal to taking refuge [in the Triple Gem];
One’s single lifetime will have passed not in vain."
If the two syllables "Dharma" reach one's tongue,
equaling those who take refuge, one’s life will not have been spent in vain;
if the two syllables "Saṃgha" reach one's tongue, [the same shall hold true].
"Taking refuge in them as they do, one will not have lived this life in vain.
Furthermore, a verse says:
"If one does not know the names of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, that person is most base and thus gains nothing."
"Transmigrating through the cycle of rebirth for a long time, it is like a kāśī flower remaining suspended in space.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the assembly of bhikṣus, Śakra, Lord of Devas, and all the great multitude rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated, and withdrew.
The Sutra on the Devaputra Cāṇūra Receiving the Three Refuges and Attaining Liberation from the Evil Realms, as Spoken by the Buddha.
